prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP manifesto summary (circa 1999–2006)

Core purpose
- Leave the European Union, repeal the European Communities Act (1972), keep the pound permanently, and restore full UK sovereignty over laws, taxation, justice, borders, defence, agriculture and fisheries.
- Defend British common law, trial by jury and presumption of innocence. UKIP says it is non-racist and inclusive; not anti-European but anti-EU centralisation.

Economy and tax
- Global free trade: regain an independent WTO seat, deepen ties with the Commonwealth, US/NAFTA and fast-growing economies. Trade with EU to continue based on mutual interest.
- Deregulation: scrap swathes of EU-derived rules, prioritising relief for small firms; oppose compulsory metrication; reduce red tape and “gold-plating.”
- Independence Dividend: about £20bn/year from ending EU budget payments and gains from growth/deregulation, admin savings, and fisheries.
- Planned uses include: agriculture support (~£2bn), regional aid (£1bn), pensions (+£5/week; ~£2.8bn), elderly care (£0.5bn) and expat pension uprating (£0.3bn), NHS (+£2bn) and nurses’ pay (+£0.5bn), 30,000 more teachers (~£1.2bn), 25,000 more police (~£0.8bn), defence (+£2.5bn), and a 9p/litre fuel duty cut (~£3.7bn).
- Tax: raise the income tax threshold to remove ~1m low earners from tax; simplify tax (review self-assessment, consider retail sales tax in place of VAT outside EU); reform CGT/IHT, exempt main homes; resist EU tax harmonisation and preserve zero-rated VAT items.

Money and monetary policy
- Keep sterling; reject the euro. Retain Bank of England operational independence with low, stable inflation focus.

Health, welfare, pensions
- NHS: decentralise management; restore “matron” model; prioritise patient care over bureaucracy; improve nurse pay and practical training; welcome appropriate non-EU recruitment.
- Welfare: simplify benefits, make work pay, curb fraud; consider basic income in limited cases (e.g., long-term unemployed, single parents).
- Family: restore married couple’s allowance for households with children under 18.
- Pensions: +£5/week, more elderly care support, unfreeze expat pensions; explore diverting part of NI into personal pension funds (existing pensioners unaffected).

Education
- Greater school autonomy, selection/streaming permitted; target class sizes under 25 via 30,000 extra teachers; elevate technical/vocational routes; consider vouchers; tackle politicised teaching; end sale of playing fields.

Transport and environment
- Integrated transport; case-by-case approach to ownership (oppose partial Tube sell-off); invest in bypasses, maintenance, cycle lanes; cut fuel duty; oppose Climate Change Levy.
- Decentralise environmental enforcement to accountable local teams; clear GMO labelling and protection for organic farming; support renewables (biofuels, wind, solar, wave, hydrogen).

Home affairs, crime, immigration
- Oppose EU “Corpus Juris” and Europol overreach; repeal and re-enact the Human Rights Act to align with UK common law; reject the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights.
- Policing: more officers, high-visibility local policing, less bureaucracy; deterrent sentences with rehabilitation alternatives for non-violent crime.
- Immigration: skills-based, firm but humane; restore fair treatment for Commonwealth family reunion; speed asylum decisions with supervised reception centres; seek reform of the 1951 Refugee Convention.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Leave CAP; introduce voluntary Land Management Contracts paying farmers for agreed environmental/social outcomes; support organics and high animal welfare; enable diversification and farm shops; balanced access/rights to roam.
- Fisheries: exit CFP; assert exclusive rights (up to 200 miles) with conservation zones; manage stocks on a Norway-style model.

Defence and foreign policy
- Reinforce all services (+£2.5bn), reverse politicised management; buy best-value kit (often US); leave EU Rapid Reaction Force; anchor security in NATO; reform aid to empower local communities; back Council of Europe cooperation.

Constitution and governance
- New UK Bill of Rights forbidding any transfer of sovereignty; strengthen Parliament and Select Committees; oppose state funding of parties; maintain bicameralism; review devolution (e.g., Wales referendum), resolve West Lothian question; restore county powers/boundaries; enable local referenda; reject any EU constitution superseding UK law.
